verdict.rationale: vLLM's own docs state support for NVIDIA GPUs and AMD GPUs, plus hardware plugins for other accelerators such as Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, Huawei Ascend and MetaX GPU, so multi-vendor execution is clearly documented. The 'vendor-specific acceleration kernels' part is only implied, through vendor formats like NVFP4 and per-scheme backend overrides, not documented directly. missing for 10: explicit documentation of vendor-specific kernels (e.g., CUDA vs ROCm attention/GEMM kernels), per-vendor performance or feature parity details, independent hands-on corroboration on non-NVIDIA hardware

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run models on NVIDIA, AMD, or other GPU vendors using vendor-specific acceleration kernels

citations.quote: Support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs. Additionally, diverse hardware plugins such as Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, IBM Spyre, Huawei Ascend, Rebellions NPU, Apple Silicon, MetaX GPU, and more.
Run any model on any hardware.
use `linear_backend_per_quant` to override the backend for individual schemes
